At the same time, potatoes release moisture, creating a damp environment that can cause onions to soften and develop mould. When kept together, this exchange makes both spoil faster. To help them last longer, store onions and potatoes in separate, cool, dry, and well-ventilated spots.' THIP Media Take: The claim that storing potatoes and onions together can kill a child is false. There is no scientific evidence to support it. While it's true that these vegetables should be stored separately for better shelf life, they do not release toxic chemicals that can kill. The post uses scary visuals and unverified science to spread fear. Always check facts before believing or sharing health claims online.

claim_text: The Head of the World Health Organization admits he has not received the COVID vaccine / Head of World Health Organization admits he's unvaccinated
doctor_explanation: No. There is no evidence to confirm that the WHO's chief is still unvaccinated as of September 2023. We have previously found a similar claim circulating on social media in August 2022, which related to the same video featuring Tedros, as mentioned in the claim within this story. While attempting this fact-check story, we realized that social media posts referring to this same video lack the necessary context for users to understand Tedros' vaccination status as of September 2023. In our previous story, we have shown that the video clip in question is extracted from an interview with Tedros, conducted on June 12, 2021, by Jon Cohen, a writer for the publication Science. In the clip shared on X, Tedros, originally from eastern Africa, mentioned that he delayed his vaccination in protest of the delay in COVID-19 vaccination for people living in Africa and other low-income regions. This video clip is sourced from the HBO Originals documentary titled 'How to Survive a Pandemic.' A transcript of the interview indicates that Tedros mentioned receiving his vaccination in 2021. Evidence confirming Tedros' vaccination in May 2021, can be found on his official account on the X platform. This is not the first instance where we've encountered inconsistent claims alleging that the WHO's chief has made inaccurate statements concerning COVID-19. We have previously debunked a claim that WHO's chief stated that COVID-19 vaccine booster shots are intended to harm children.

claim_text: Dr Naresh Trehan is endorsing a home remedy to cure diabetes, and pharmaceutical companies are hiding natural cures to make money off people's illness.
doctor_explanation:
The viral video claiming Dr Naresh Trehan is endorsing a quick diabetes remedy is confirmed to be fake. The video was altered using AI technology, showing clear signs of manipulation such as mismatched lip-syncing and unnatural facial expressions. Dr Naresh Trehan does not appear to speak or act as he normally does. A search related to Dr Trehan on social media and a review of trusted medical websites found no credible information supporting the claim. THIP has contacted Dr Trehan about the misuse of his image and is awaiting his response. The Facebook video does not offer a specific diabetes remedy; it asks viewers to click a link, but the link only displays Spanish text about the benefits of a healthy diet with no actionable information — this is classic clickbait designed to mislead. Similar AI-manipulated videos were found featuring Rajat Sharma and Dr Ramakanta Panda promoting a hypertension cure, and another featuring Dr Devi Shetty promoting a diabetes cure in just 37 hours, both leading to similar dead links with no information. Another video featured news anchor Sudhir Chaudhary promoting a quick fix for diabetes in just seven days. When clicked, the link leads to Spanish text stating: 'A healthy diet provides protection against malnutrition in all its forms, as well as non-communicable diseases' — general diet information, not a diabetes cure.

Dr Aashirwad Pawar, Diabetologist, Sai Aashirwad Hospital, Mumbai, states: 'There is no one-step cure for diabetes. While Type 2 diabetes can often be managed—and even sent into remission—through lifestyle changes, medication, and sometimes surgery, it isn't cured in the traditional sense. Home remedies, like certain herbs or foods, may support blood sugar control but cannot replace medical treatment. Diabetes management requires a comprehensive, individualised approach under medical guidance.'

Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says: 'Diabetes is a long-term condition that needs ongoing management. While certain lifestyle changes, such as a balanced diet and regular physical activity, can help control blood sugar levels, there is no medical evidence to support the claim that any home remedy can cure diabetes. Effective management involves a combination of medication, dietary adjustments, and regular monitoring.'

Dr Anusha Dewan, Practising General Physician and Public Health Professional, Jeevan Anmol Hospital, New Delhi, states: 'Managing the condition involves consistent treatment with prescribed medications, lifestyle modifications, and regular check-ups. While some home remedies may offer benefits in controlling blood sugar to a limited extent, they cannot replace medical treatment or cure diabetes. The only proven way to manage diabetes is through evidence-based, long-term care.'

Regarding the conspiracy that pharmaceutical companies are hiding natural cures: no solid evidence supports this claim. Respected health organisations and independent scientists conduct diabetes research worldwide, and if a simple natural cure for diabetes existed, the medical community would widely recognise and support it.

Diabetes cannot be cured with a one-step remedy. It is a lifelong condition managed through lifestyle changes, medications, and sometimes insulin. There is no 'quick fix.' Medical experts recommend long-term, evidence-based approaches to manage diabetes.

claim_text: Cancer is Not a Disease but a Survival Mechanism Trying to Save Your Life. Tumors develop as the body's way of coping with underlying toxicity, emotional stress, or metabolic imbalances. Doctors make money off unhealthy humans. A biopsy pokes the tumor and allows cancer cells and toxins to spread throughout the body. Most people don't die from cancer — they die from the treatment of cancer. So when cancer appears to spread after a biopsy, doctors then charge more money for radiation, chemotherapy, etc.
doctor_explanation: Dr. C N Patil, HOD and Lead Consultant - Medical Oncology & Haemato-Oncology, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore, stated: "The claim that 'cancer is not a disease but a survival mechanism trying to save your life' is a controversial idea promoted by some alternative health advocates, notably Andreas Moritz in his book Cancer Is Not a Disease - It's a Survival Mechanism. This perspective suggests that tumors develop as the body's way of coping with underlying toxicity, emotional stress, or metabolic imbalances rather than being a harmful disease in itself. However, this view is not supported by mainstream medical science. Cancer is, in fact, a disease characterized by uncontrolled cell growth due to genetic mutations. These mutations can result from various factors, including exposure to carcinogens (such as tobacco smoke, radiation, and certain chemicals), lifestyle choices (like diet and physical activity), and genetic predisposition. When normal regulatory mechanisms in the body fail, cancer cells multiply uncontrollably, forming tumors that can invade nearby tissues and spread to distant parts of the body through metastasis. The idea that cancer is a survival mechanism comes from observations that some tumors seem to emerge in response to chronic stress or persistent inflammation. For example, wound healing and tissue regeneration share some molecular pathways with cancer development, leading to hypotheses that cancer might have evolved from ancient repair mechanisms. However, just because cancer shares similarities with wound healing does not mean it is a beneficial or protective process. Unlike normal wound healing, cancer cells continue to divide uncontrollably, leading to the destruction of healthy tissue. Moreover, medical research has shown that cancer, if left untreated, leads to significant harm, including organ failure, pain, and death. While some early-stage cancers can be slow-growing and manageable, many aggressive forms require medical intervention to prevent life-threatening complications. Modern oncology has made significant advancements in understanding cancer biology, leading to targeted treatments, immunotherapies, and precision medicine approaches that improve survival rates. It is crucial to rely on scientific evidence rather than unverified claims when discussing cancer. The idea that cancer is a survival mechanism may mislead people into avoiding proper medical treatment. While lifestyle changes, stress management, and a healthy diet can support overall well-being and may reduce cancer risk, they are not substitutes for evidence-based cancer treatment. In conclusion, cancer is a disease caused by genetic mutations leading to uncontrolled cell growth. The claim that it is merely a survival mechanism lacks scientific support and could be dangerous if it leads people to reject necessary medical care." Dr Sumanth Kumar Mallupattu, Consultant - Medical Oncology, CARE Hospitals, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, further explained: "Cancer is a disease caused by genetic mutations that lead to uncontrolled cell growth. While some claim that cancer is a 'survival mechanism,' this is a dangerous misinterpretation of science. Left untreated, cancerous cells invade healthy tissues, impair organ function, and can be life-threatening. Early detection is critical because cancers in early stages are often more localized and respond better to treatment, whether it's surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy. Advanced cancers, on the other hand, become harder to treat and can spread (metastasize) to other organs, reducing survival rates. Misinformation like this can discourage people from seeking timely medical intervention, which can make a crucial difference in their prognosis." On the biopsy claim specifically: The American Cancer Society noted, "While cancer spread after a biopsy can technically happen, it's important to remember that it's extremely rare. The benefits of getting a biopsy far outweigh the minimal risk of cancer spread." In a review conducted by Dimitrios Volanis et al., researchers analyzed prior studies and concluded that needle tract seeding was reported to be below 1%. A study published in The Cancers reviewed existing research on tumor seeding following breast needle biopsies and found that undergoing a needle biopsy does not significantly influence the risk of breast cancer recurrence, metastasis, or overall survival outcomes. Therefore, the biopsy-spreads-cancer claim is also FALSE.

claim_text: If you are troubled by tooth decay and bad breath, then you must try this powerful home remedy. Simply take cloves and cinnamon, grind them into a powder, and mix one teaspoon of clove powder, one teaspoon of cinnamon powder, and one teaspoon of coconut oil in a bowl. Apply this mixture to your teeth, especially where there is pain, and massage gently with your finger. After just 5 minutes, rinse your mouth with water and feel the difference—no pain, no bad breath, and no tooth decay.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Prakhar Pragya, MDS, Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopaedics, Consultant Orthodontics at South Delhi Region, told Medical Dialogues: 'While clove, cinnamon, and coconut oil have natural benefits like reducing bacteria and soothing discomfort, they cannot magically eliminate tooth pain, decay, or bad breath in just 5 minutes. Tooth decay is permanent and needs professional dental care. Good oral hygiene, regular brushing, flossing, and dental check-ups, along with addressing underlying issues, are the real solutions for a healthy smile.' Dr. Ritika Punjabi, MDS, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMFS), Senior Lecturer, ITS Dental College, Muradnagar, added: 'Natural remedies like cloves, cinnamon, and coconut oil can offer temporary relief, but they are not a quick fix for tooth decay, pain, or bad breath. Tooth decay doesn't heal on its own, and bad breath often signals an underlying issue. The best way to keep your teeth healthy is to brush twice daily, floss, stay hydrated, and visit your dentist regularly. There's no shortcut to good oral health.'

Scientific evidence cited: The article reviews multiple studies showing that while these ingredients have individual benefits, none support the 5-minute elimination claim. A study in the International Journal of Dentistry found that clove oil-treated teeth exhibited reduced de-calcification and may support re-mineralization, but does not claim clove oil can eliminate tooth decay within 5 minutes. A review in the World Journal of Pharmaceutical Research states that chewing cloves can help reduce bad breath and tooth pain but only provides temporary relief and does not mention effectiveness within 5 minutes. A review in the journal Molecules highlights that cinnamon has antibacterial properties against oral pathogens linked to caries or tooth decay, helping in caries prevention and reducing bad breath, but does not state that cinnamon can cure or eliminate bad breath or tooth decay once formed, nor claims effectiveness within 5 minutes. A review in the AL-AZHAR Dental Journal mentions that ancient civilizations used cinnamon to treat tooth pain and combat bad breath, but this claim is anecdotal and lacks scientific experimental evidence. A systematic review published in Heliyon suggests that oil pulling with coconut oil may help improve oral hygiene, but does not state that coconut oil can eliminate tooth pain, tooth decay, or bad breath within 5 minutes.

Tooth decay (dental caries) is an irreversible bacterial disease that leads to breakdown of the tooth's mineral content and destruction of its organic structure (Shafer, 1993). It is caused by cariogenic bacteria like Streptococcus mutans, which produce acids that erode enamel. The four key factors in caries formation are bacterial plaque, fermentable sugars, tooth structure, and time. Tooth pain (odontogenic pain) originates from teeth or surrounding structures and can be caused by pulp inflammation from cavities, dental abscesses, bruxism, or sensitivity. Bad breath (halitosis) has multiple causes: approximately 80–85% of cases originate inside the mouth (gum infections, cavities, dry mouth, poorly fitted dentures); other causes include digestive problems, acid reflux (GERD), H. pylori infection (Kinberg et al., 2010 found over half of 94 halitosis patients had stomach-related issues), and habits like smoking and alcohol. The article concludes that studies acknowledge the role of clove, cinnamon, and coconut oil in reducing tooth decay, pain, and bad breath, but none confirm their ability—individually or combined—to completely eliminate these issues within 5 minutes.

claim_text: Buying ripe bananas. Green stalk with brown spots means they were chemically ripened. Black stalk.. naturally ripened.
doctor_explanation: No, the presence of a green stalk or brown spots on a banana does not necessarily indicate that it has been chemically ripened. It is not possible to visually analyze that a banana or any other fruit has been chemically ripened. Some bananas are picked when they are still green and then allowed to ripen naturally during transportation and storage. These bananas may have a green stalk when they are purchased, but they have not been chemically ripened. When bananas ripen, their starches break down into sugars, making them sweet and better to eat. Its true that certain chemicals are sometimes used to accelerate the ripening process. Ethylene gas, acetylene gas liberated from calcium carbide, and ethephon are some of the commercial ripening agents used. According to studies, bananas treated with chemicals to induce ripening show no significant difference in biochemical composition and sensory quality compared to naturally ripened bananas. However, naturally ripened bananas are generally regarded as having superior sensory characteristics when compared to chemically treated fruits. But, there is no visual test to assess if a banana has been chemically treated or naturally ripened. Moreover, the spot patterns on bananas are a striking case of biological pattern formation and as a qualitative ripeness indicator. Bruising on bananas happen as ripening advances and they become progressively softer and will readily bruise if handled improperly. According to Japanese Scientific Research, fully ripe banana with dark patches on yellow skin produces a substance called TNF (Tumor Necrosis Factor) which has the ability to combat abnormal cells. The more dark spots it has, the higher its immunity enhancement will be. Hence, the riper the banana the better the anti-cancer quality.

claim_text: Placing chopped onions on feet and covering it with socks can cure Pneumonia. Flavonoids, absorbed through the pores of the feet, help to remove phlegm from the lungs and treat pneumonia due to their properties.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Kamal Kant Kohli, Chest Specialist, explained that pneumonia risk factors include medical conditions (chronic lung diseases like COPD, diabetes, weakened immune systems from HIV/AIDS), health behaviours (cigarette smoking, substance abuse), and environmental factors (exposure to chemicals, pollutants, toxic fumes including secondhand smoke). He stated that pneumonia is a serious respiratory infection requiring proper medical treatment. Dr. Mrigakshi Agarwal, Pulmonologist at Sanjeevan Hospital, New Delhi, clarified that placing onions under the feet and covering them with socks does not cure pneumonia. She stated this practice is a folk remedy without any scientific basis or clinical evidence supporting its effectiveness against pneumonia. She explained that onions contain antioxidants and compounds with anti-inflammatory and possibly expectorant properties that may help alleviate respiratory symptoms — only when consumed — but placing onion on feet and covering with socks does not help and lacks scientific evidence. She emphasised that it is essential to consult healthcare professionals for proper diagnosis and treatment rather than relying on unproven home remedies. While some studies indicate that onions have antimicrobial and possible bronchodilatory effects (e.g., a study by Jorge García-García et al. indicating possible bronchodilatory and preventive effects of onion and quercetin on asthma and virus-infected flu symptoms), and garlic/onions possess antimicrobial properties against microorganisms causing pneumonia (Bryan-Thomas et al.), and a study by Beigoli et al. suggests onion compounds may help reduce inflammation and improve immune responses — these studies emphasise potential of extracts in preventative care rather than as a cure for existing conditions. Nowhere in any cited study does the research support that onions can cure pneumonia or that the treatment modality includes placing onions on feet and wearing socks. There is no scientific basis for the claim that flavonoids can be absorbed through the pores of the feet — the skin does not absorb nutrients in this manner. Despite in vitro studies showing antimicrobial and bronchodilatory properties, the claim lacks scientific and consensus evidence in the medical fraternity to support its effectiveness in treating pneumonia.

claim_text: Anulom Vilom (alternate nostril breathing) can cure migraine in 3 minutes and bring high blood pressure under control in 5 minutes. The claim is based on the idea that the right nostril is associated with the Surya Nadi (sun channel) which generates heat, while the left nostril activates the Chandra Nadi (moon channel) which brings coolness and calmness — so breathing only through the left nostril can stimulate cooling energy, relieve headache, ease migraine, and normalize high BP.
doctor_explanation:
Both consulted doctors categorically rejected the claim that Anulom Vilom can cure migraine in 3 minutes or normalize high blood pressure in 5 minutes.

Dr. Avinash Kulkarni, Consultant Neurologist at Gleneagles BGS Hospital, stated: 'The short answer is no, because both blood pressure and migraine are chronic conditions — there is no concept of a complete cure. Now, is the claim entirely false? Not really. It is partially true. Breathing patterns play an important role. The way we breathe influences changes in the brain. They are interconnected. In patients with migraine, certain breathing patterns — especially the Indian practice of anulom-vilom or pranayama — have been shown to alter brain chemistry in a way that reduces headache episodes. This can decrease the overall frequency of attacks. However, it does not cure migraine. The same applies to blood pressure. Research has shown that deeper, slower breathing lowers blood pressure. During anulom-vilom, one breathes deeply and the number of breaths per minute comes down. This calm breathing pattern leads to a reduction in blood pressure to near-normal levels. But this effect is transient. It does not mean blood pressure is cured. Patients should therefore not believe claims that migraine or hypertension can be cured, nor should they stop their prescribed medicines in favor of breathing exercises alone. Doing so can result in serious complications such as stroke or heart attack. Breathing exercises like anulom-vilom should be considered only as a supportive measure, to be practiced alongside proper medical management under the guidance of a neurologist or cardiologist.'

Dr. Umesh Tukaram, MBBS, MD (General Medicine), DM (Neurology), Clinical Director & Senior Consultant Neurology at CARE Hospitals, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, added: 'Anulom Vilom, also known as alternate nostril breathing, is a yoga technique that is believed to calm the nervous system, reduce stress, and improve overall well-being. Regular practice is often said to help in controlling blood pressure and reducing the frequency and intensity of migraine attacks. However, it is very important to clarify that no breathing exercise, including Anulom Vilom, can cure migraine within three minutes or normalize high blood pressure in five minutes. Migraine and hypertension are medical conditions influenced by multiple factors such as genetics, lifestyle, diet, and stress. While yoga and breathing exercises can be excellent complementary therapies, they should never replace medical treatment. If someone is experiencing frequent migraines or high blood pressure, I strongly recommend consulting a qualified medical professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.'

The article cites WHO's definition of hypertension as blood pressure consistently at or above 140/90 mmHg, noting that untreated hypertension can lead to serious health problems and does not have a permanent cure — it can only be managed with lifestyle changes and prescribed medications. Migraine is described as a neurological condition with a genetic basis, marked by repeated episodes of moderate to severe headache, usually one-sided, accompanied by nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia; attacks may last hours to days and are a major contributor to disability.

Scientific evidence cited in the article includes: a study in Acta Scientific Medical Sciences showing Anulom Vilom boosts lung function, increases vital capacity and breath-holding time, and strengthens respiratory muscles, supporting better cardio-respiratory performance and higher energy levels; a study in the International Journal of Science and Healthcare Research finding that four weeks of regular practice reduced certain cardiovascular parameters in hypertensive patients (but with no evidence of effect within 5 minutes); and a study by Anjana Kaushal et al. (PMC10666878) reporting that pranayama may complement migraine treatment by reducing headache severity and frequency and shortening episode duration — but with no evidence supporting a 3-minute cure.

The article explicitly states that while Anulom Vilom may support respiratory health, aid in hypertension management over time, and yoga can complement migraine treatment, there is no scientific evidence that it can cure migraines in 3 minutes or lower high blood pressure in 5 minutes.

claim_text: An Instagram post suggests that clove water, if used topically, can lighten your skin color.
doctor_explanation: Skin colour is determined mainly by melanin, a pigment produced by specialised skin cells. To truly "whiten" or lighten skin, something would need to safely reduce melanin production or distribution in human skin and clove water has not been proven to do this. There are no well-designed human clinical studies showing that clove water spray can lighten skin tone. Most claims online are based on personal anecdotes or misunderstandings of laboratory research, not real-world evidence. Dr Sachin Gupta, MBBS, MD (Dermatology and Venereology, AIIMS Delhi), Amrita Hospital, cautions: "In dermatology, 'natural' does not automatically mean safe or effective. Substances that appear gentle or harmless can still pose risks to the skin." For any persistent or concerning skin issue, consulting a qualified dermatologist remains the safest option. Dermatologists design treatment plans based on scientific evidence, clinical experience, and a clear understanding of individual skin physiology. This personalised, evidence-based approach helps ensure that skin treatments are both effective and appropriate for a person's specific needs. Some laboratory (test-tube) studies have explored clove extracts and compounds like eugenol for their effect on melanin-producing cells. In very controlled lab conditions, certain extracts showed an ability to influence melanin pathways. However, lab studies are not the same as skincare evidence. These experiments use isolated cells, precise concentrations, and purified compounds. Human skin is far more complex, it has protective barriers, blood flow, immune responses, and constant exposure to sunlight and pollution. What works in a petri dish does not automatically work on a face. Even more importantly, not all research points in the same direction. Some experimental studies suggest that eugenol can stimulate melanocyte activity under certain conditions, which could theoretically increase pigmentation rather than reduce it. This inconsistency alone makes clove a poor candidate for "whitening." Dr. Annusuiya Gohil, an MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, also explains that skin pigmentation is largely influenced by genetic makeup and environmental exposure. Although various measures can help improve overall skin brightness and appearance, a person's natural skin pigmentation cannot be changed, only enhanced or managed to some extent. Clove contains eugenol, a biologically active compound that can irritate the skin. When applied repeatedly especially in homemade, unmeasured concentrations it may cause skin irritation. When skin becomes inflamed, the body responds by increasing melanin production during healing. This process, called post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, is a common cause of stubborn dark patches particularly in medium to deeper skin tones. Ironically, a remedy used for "whitening" can leave skin looking darker and patchier over time. While clove oil is more concentrated and clearly risky, clove water is still unpredictable. There is no standard recipe. One person may soak two cloves, another may boil ten. Spray frequency, skin sensitivity, sun exposure, and existing acne or damage all change how skin reacts. "Natural" does not mean gentle. Many plant compounds are potent precisely because they are biologically active. Without proper formulation and testing, even diluted preparations can cause harm. Some people notice a brief tightening or refreshing sensation after using clove water. This is not whitening. It is usually due to mild astringent or irritant effects that temporarily reduce oil or tighten pores. Once washed off or once irritation sets in the effect disappears. Temporary brightness is often mistaken for long-term skin improvement, which fuels misleading claims online. Evidence-based skincare works better and is safer. If the goal is an even, healthy-looking complexion (not changing natural skin colour), professional guidance and evidence-based skincare products are far more effective than DIY remedies.

claim_text: Covid-19 vaccine weakens people's immune systems, like immunotherapy. A British funeral director, John O'Looney, claims in a video: 'So, they've had the jabs (Covid Vaccines) maybe six to eight months ago and it's been eating away at their immune system – and now they're struggling to fight off things like the common cold.' He further adds '(Like cancer patients on chemotherapy,) they've got no immune system – a basic common cold or flu can kill them. And this is what we're seeing now in these jab recipients up and down the country.'
doctor_explanation: No. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention states that 'Exact vaccine ingredients vary by manufacturer. Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines also contain messenger RNA (mRNA) and the Johnson & Johnson/Janssen COVID-19 vaccine contains a harmless version of a virus unrelated to the virus that causes COVID-19. These give instructions to cells in your body to create an immune response. This response helps protect you from getting sick with COVID-19 in the future.' After the body produces an immune response, it discards all the vaccine ingredients just as it would discard any information that cells no longer need. This process is a part of normal body functioning. No. There is no scientific evidence that suggests that vaccines alter or weaken immunity systems. Rather, vaccines have received support from the scientific communities across the world for their ability to prevent diseases. Dr. Paul Offit from the Vaccine Education Center, in a video for The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, states that, 'The way these vaccines work is just a fragment of messenger RNA, which we have in our cells all the time. Because of the messenger RNA, the vaccine enters your cells and then essentially is translated to a protein, in this case the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which sits on the surface of the cell. So, the cell makes this spike protein. While the cell is making the spike proteins, it's making a variety of other proteins using messenger RNA, none of which affect the immune system negatively; none of which sort of downregulate the immune system; none of which cause a perturbation of the immune system.' Therefore, there is no reason to believe that the SARS-CoV-2 vaccines would weaken your immune system. And there's certainly no evidence that it does that. Rather it strengthens the immune system as they give you antibodies against this virus. Hence, the claim is false.

claim_text: An Instagram reel suggests that morning tea is as harmful as poison. It argues that tea, especially when consumed with sugar and milk, feeds bad bacteria in the gut. The post further claims that tea does not clean the stomach as believed but instead triggers dependency.
doctor_explanation: Morning tea cannot be considered poison. There is no scientific evidence or medical backing for this claim. When consumed in moderation, tea is safe and can even be good for your health. Poison refers to things that can harm or kill you, and tea is definitely not one of those. The claim seems to exaggerate some of the potential downsides of tea, like adding sugar or milk. But even with these, they're not harmful if you consume them in moderation. In fact, a 2017 study found that drinking tea and milk can lower the risk of oral cancer, especially when both are consumed together. The benefits were more noticeable in older adults, urban residents, and men with a healthy weight. Another study from 2007, found that brewing black tea for longer increases its health benefits, such as antioxidants and catechins. Adding milk doesn't affect these benefits. Overall, the benefits of tea far outweigh any risks when it's part of a balanced diet. Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, says, 'Tea contains polyphenols, which contribute to its safety and health benefits. Compared to coffee, tea generally contains lower levels of caffeine, making it a suitable option for many individuals. It can be enjoyed in the morning with added sugar and milk or prepared according to personal preferences. Claims suggesting that tea is harmful or poisonous are unfounded. For those who experience gastric issues, it is advisable to consume milder tea varieties and avoid boiling them for prolonged periods. Ultimately, morning tea can be a delightful and healthful choice.' Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, says, 'Morning tea is definitely not 'poison.' In fact, it's a drink that many people enjoy for its refreshing taste and health benefits. Tea contains antioxidants that can support heart health and protect cells from damage. The concern with adding too much sugar or milk is that it can increase your calorie intake, but in moderation, tea is a healthy choice, not something to fear.' The claim that tea feeds bad bacteria in the gut is misleading. While milk and sugar can influence gut bacteria, their effects depend on the overall diet. Research shows dairy, like milk, can benefit gut health, while excessive sugar can disrupt it. However, adding a teaspoon of sugar to tea is unlikely to cause significant harm, and individual responses to milk can vary. On the contrary, tea contains polyphenols, which have prebiotic properties. These compounds promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria, supporting digestive health. Research shows that tea, especially green tea, can positively impact gut microbiota. Tea does not 'clean' the stomach, but this is not its purpose. The belief that tea acts as a stomach cleanser is a misconception. Tea stimulates digestion and can have a mild laxative effect for some, but it does not physically cleanse the stomach. Warm water, as suggested in the claim, may help with hydration but does not 'break any programme' or replace tea's unique properties, as claimed in the video. Tea offers several health benefits due to its rich polyphenol content. Green tea is abundant in catechins, which are powerful antioxidants, while black tea contains theaflavins with anti-inflammatory and heart-protective properties. However, excessive tea consumption, especially with high amounts of sugar or milk, can contribute to calorie intake and potentially affect health negatively. Moderation is key.

claim_text: By drinking slimming tea, one can reduce 5 kg in ten days
doctor_explanation: The video promotes a slimming tea without disclosing its ingredients, despite efforts to contact the seller. It asserts that consuming the tea will result in a weight loss of 5 kilograms within 10 days. Losing 5kg (11 pounds) in just 10 days solely by adding slimming tea to your diet is highly unlikely and not recommended. While slimming teas may offer some benefits such as temporary water weight loss or appetite suppression, the amount of weight lost is typically minimal and not primarily fat loss. For significant weight loss, especially within such a short timeframe, it's essential to focus on comprehensive lifestyle changes. Relying solely on slimming tea for weight loss can be risky and may not lead to sustainable results. Additionally, drastic weight loss in a short period can have adverse effects on health, including muscle loss, nutrient deficiencies, and metabolic disturbances. Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda (ĀCĀRA), explains that according to Ayurveda, obesity is a challenging condition to address. Ayurvedic texts even assert that it's nearly incurable – 'na hi sthulasya bheshajam'. There are no magical solutions for obesity, and it can't be remedied by a single internal or external medicine. Instead, treatment primarily focuses on managing stress, adopting a suitable lifestyle, and following a specific diet. Medications, whether internal or external, play a supportive role. The effectiveness of the treatment is enhanced when patients adhere to a comprehensive, personalized approach to address obesity. Nutritionist Dr. Swati Dave expressed disbelief and stated that it's ridiculous that people trust such gimmicks. She emphasized that slimming tea is not a miracle weight reduction drink; it does not burn fat or promote weight loss on its own. Without knowing the ingredients, consuming ordinary spices, including green tea, daily may not be safe. Trusting such products is absurd. Dr. Dave stressed that there are no shortcuts to losing weight. Rapid weight loss leads to rapid weight regain. Misinformation from unprofessional sources can lead individuals to make unhealthy lifestyle choices, adopt unproven remedies, delay seeking proper medical advice, and contribute to anxiety, unnecessary money spending, stress, and unnecessary worry.

claim_text: Keeping your hair wet after bathing will cause a cold.
doctor_explanation: No. The common cold is caused by viruses. Keeping the hair wet, being in cool temperature with wet hair, sleeping with wet hair – all these will not cause a common cold. This is an old myth that has been debunked by medical professionals for years. Dr. Deepanshu Khanna, MBBS, MD, DNB(General medicine) says, "These beliefs are all misconceptions. Although these beliefs are amongst us for ages, there is still no scientific basis behind these beliefs. The cause of fever or a cold is infectious virus or bacteria, and also dust in the wind which causes allergy-related issues." Dr. Khanna explains further, "You may catch a cold if you eat something unhygienic, without washing your hands or from eating something that causes allergic reactions in your body. But showering with cold water or wet hair after a shower is not the cause of catching a cold or fever. In fact, showering with cold water has some health benefits. It increases blood circulation, improves metabolism, can help reduce inflammation or deal with depression." That said, there is one isolated research that showed keeping the feet in chilled water for a long duration made participants more susceptible to catching a cold. Note, the research did not have anything to do with wet hair but just experimented with wet feet. Also, only 10% of the small group who participated in the research caught cold, and the researchers concluded, "Further studies are needed." Not exactly. Though you will not catch a cold, there can be other health issues arising due to wet hair. These can include hair damage and fungal infections including dandruff.

claim_text: The combination of coffee and baby oil can successfully clear dark circles
doctor_explanation: Dark circles, or black discolouration in the periorbital region, constitute a frequent cosmetic complaint that provides the appearance of being aged or worn out. This hyperpigmentation is usually brought on by sleep deprivation, prolonged screen time, and sun exposure which can worsen their appearance by affecting the pigmentation and circulation under the eyes. Individuals who frequently wipe their eyes and have atopic or allergy issues may also be affected. Because periorbital hyperpigmentation is influenced by both intrinsic and extrinsic sources, determining the correct underlying cause is essential for the optimal course of treatment. While the combination of baby oil and coffee is being widely promoted for clearing dark circles, its relevance is confined to social media platforms. This is primarily attributed to the fact that under-eye pigmentation is not just a single-cause cosmetic concern; its appearance is associated with several contributors, which may not be effectively addressed with a single unsupervised formulation. Coffee contains caffeine which exhibits antioxidant and vasoconstrictive characteristics. Although some clinical formulations including caffeine may show a slight decrease in puffiness and periocular hyperpigmentation, these results are restricted to small-scale controlled trials. The direct application of coffee grounds or homemade coffee pastes for dark circles is not well supported by scientific research. Additionally, excessive or improper application may irritate the delicate periocular skin due to its abrasive nature. Baby oil is pure mineral oil containing vitamin E. Even though mineral oil may work as an emollient to enhance skin barrier function and hydration by reducing transepidermal water loss, there is no clinical evidence that it alone lightens dark circles or addresses their underlying causes. Overuse of oil can also upset sensitive individuals or clog pores. Dr. Rashi Soni, a Specialist Dermatologist at Mumbai's Rashi Hospital, explains that although the aforementioned ingredients may appear to be natural substitutes, they are ineffective for removing dark circles. A number of causes, including thin skin, ageing, lack of sleep, and heredity, can cause under-eye pigmentation, which cannot be managed via home remedies alone. While certain substances might provide minor skin improvements, they don't address the root cause of the problem. Persistence, patience, and regular use of a personalised skincare routine under professional supervision are necessary for effective results. Dr. Iftekhar Khan, MD (Dermatology), an assistant professor at SMS Medical College in Jaipur, maintains that home remedies are not the best solution for addressing under-eye darkness. The skin underneath the eyes is thinner and more sensitive, which could worsen the condition. A thorough evaluation of the problem and unwavering perseverance are necessary for under-eye therapy to be successful. Unregulated solutions are discouraged by medical experts due to the complex development of under-eye pigmentation. Therefore, determining the precise underlying cause—vascular, pigmentary, structural, or a combination—is essential to effective care. Instead of following the viral trends, a dermatologist should be consulted for expert advice.

claim_text: WEF Declares Pedophilia 'Sexual Orientation' Must Be Added To LGBTQAI+. The LGBTQAI+ rainbow community must add a P according to the World Economic Forum in Davos which has declared that pedophilia is an acceptable sexual orientation that deserves respect.
doctor_explanation: This article is a general misinformation fact-check rather than a doctor-verified medical fact-check. The Fact Check section explains: What is LGBTQAI+? The term LGBTQAI+ is an inclusive acronym representing diverse sexual orientations and gender identities including Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, asexual, Intersex, and other identities. What is pedophilia? Pedophilia is a term used to describe a psychological disorder where an adult feels sexual attraction for children. This attraction is harmful and inappropriate because children cannot consent to sexual activity. It is considered a serious offence and is illegal in many places because it can lead to harm and exploitation of children. While pedophilia itself (the attraction) is not illegal, acting on those attractions by engaging in sexual activity with children is illegal in all countries. What does the WEF do? The World Economic Forum (WEF) is an organisation that brings together leaders from government, business, and academia to discuss global issues. Has the WEF actually made this declaration? No, the WEF has not made any such declaration. There is no evidence to support the claim. A search on the WEF website shows the term 'pedophilia' has not been mentioned since 2017, and even then it was used for debunking another conspiracy theory. Representatives from GLAAD, an LGBTQ+ advocacy group, attended the Davos meeting and confirmed that no such declaration was made. Such claims have absolutely no basis and go against the core values and goals of the WEF. The article also notes this website has been well-known to publish and perpetuate false information repeatedly, with THIPmedia having debunked several of their previous claims.

claim_text: Dr Anthony Fauci admitted that none of the 72 vaccines currently required for children in the U.S. have ever been safety tested.
doctor_explanation: The claim that Dr Fauci admitted to the lack of safety testing for 72 mandatory childhood vaccines is false. Vaccines undergo extensive clinical trials to ensure their safety and effectiveness before being approved by the FDA. What did Robert F. Kennedy Jr. claim about vaccine safety testing? Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a prominent anti-vaccine advocate, has repeatedly stated that vaccines for children have never undergone placebo-controlled safety trials. He claimed that Dr Fauci faced this accusation but could not provide the requested study. According to Kennedy, Fauci's lawyers allegedly admitted that no such study existed. However, this account comes directly from Kennedy himself, not from Fauci or any verified sources. It's important to note that Kennedy's claims are not based on credible evidence. Dr Fauci and his legal team did not make any formal admission regarding the testing of vaccines. Was RFK Jr. correct in claiming that not one of the 72 childhood vaccines has been tested in placebo-controlled, pre-licensing trials? No, that claim is false. Vaccines approved for children in the United States undergo extensive safety and efficacy testing, including pre-licensing clinical trials, some of which are placebo-controlled. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requires all vaccines to pass through Phase I–III trials before licensure. Did Dr Fauci or his legal team ever admit that RFK Jr. was correct about vaccine safety testing in a lawsuit? No, there is no evidence of such an admission. There is no public legal record or credible documentation confirming that Dr Anthony Fauci or his lawyers conceded that RFK Jr. was correct. If such an admission had occurred in court, it would be a matter of public record and widely covered by mainstream and legal media. During our research, we found a media report on Dr Fauci's response to RFK Jr.'s remarks about him, which simply stated that the claims made by RFK Jr. have no scientific basis. Dr Fauci has consistently emphasised the importance of vaccine safety and the careful testing process vaccines go through. Similarly, we have seen claims which suggest SV40 is present in experimental vaccines and it causes cancer. However, this is not supported by evidence. Is it true that vaccine manufacturers face no liability and that childhood vaccines aren't properly safety tested? Partially true but highly misleading. Vaccine manufacturers are protected from most direct liability through the National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act of 1986, which created the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP). However, this legal protection does not mean vaccines skip safety testing. What do the CDC and FDA say about vaccine testing and approval? The CDC and FDA make it clear that vaccines undergo a rigorous approval process to ensure their safety. The FDA oversees the approval of vaccines and ensures each vaccine meets strict safety standards during production and after its release to the public. Additionally, various surveillance systems monitor the safety of vaccines after approval. The CDC highlights that vaccines are one of the most effective tools for preventing disease. They save millions of lives each year and prevent the spread of various infections. Is The People's Voice a reliable source of information? No, The People's Voice has been associated with publishing misleading or false information. This site has promoted conspiracy theories and misinterpreted studies. We have previously debunked several of its claims including that the WHO ordered lockdowns for a deadly monkeypox strain and that an AHA report confirmed COVID-19 vaccines cause fatal heart defects.

claim_text: Drinking clove water for two weeks before bed can shrink belly fat or give you a flatter tummy.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific proof that clove water reduces belly fat. Body fat, especially abdominal fat, is stored and lost based on overall calorie balance, hormones, genetics, physical activity, sleep, and stress levels. No drink can selectively target fat from the stomach area. Cloves contain bioactive compounds such as eugenol, flavonoids, and phenolic acids. These compounds have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which are beneficial for general health. However, none of these substances have been shown in human studies to break down fat cells or increase fat loss, particularly from the abdomen. Claims of spot fat reduction are a common myth in nutrition science. Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Prep Coach, explains that long-term loss of abdominal fat comes from consistent, science-backed habits rather than quick fixes. This includes a small, sustainable reduction in calories instead of extreme dieting, combining cardio with strength training, and eating enough protein and fibre to help control hunger. He also highlights the importance of sleep and stress management, as hormones like cortisol and insulin play a role in where fat is stored. He notes that core exercises can strengthen muscles and improve posture, making the midsection appear firmer, but they do not specifically burn belly fat. He emphasises keeping expectations grounded, real changes in health and body shape take time, and steady, manageable progress is both safer and more effective in the long run. Clove water may help reduce bloating, which can make the stomach appear flatter for a short time. Cloves have traditionally been used to support digestion because they may stimulate digestive enzymes and reduce gas formation in the gut. If someone experiences frequent bloating due to heavy meals, slow digestion, or excess gas, drinking warm clove water might ease discomfort. When bloating reduces, the abdomen can look less distended. However, this effect is cosmetic and short-lived. It does not reflect fat loss or a real reduction in waist size. Dr Durga Priyadarshini R, PhD (Nutrition), says, Cloves have compounds with mild digestive-supportive properties, and traditional use suggests they might help relieve occasional gas or bloating, but this is largely based on historical practice and small, subjective studies, not robust clinical proof. There is no high-quality research showing that cloves are effective in reducing bloating as a standalone therapy. Any benefit people feel is more likely due to warm liquid consumption, placebo response, or general soothing effects. Cloves should not be relied upon as a therapeutic agent for chronic gastrointestinal conditions, and claims that they fix bloating or heal digestion are not scientifically substantiated. Improved digestion does not equal weight loss. While cloves may help relieve mild indigestion, gas, or nausea, they do not alter how many calories the body absorbs or burns. Weight loss occurs when the body consistently uses more energy than it consumes. Clove water does not suppress appetite in a clinically meaningful way, nor does it increase energy expenditure. Dr Almas Fatma, General Physician, Navi Mumbai, highlighted that Some research suggests clove or clove-water infusions may help mild digestive discomfort like gas and bloating. While cloves have anti-inflammatory and carminative properties, most evidence comes from concentrated extracts, not clove water. Any relief is likely mild and symptomatic rather than a proven therapeutic effect. Clove water made using one or two cloves is generally safe for healthy adults when consumed occasionally. However, drinking it daily or in concentrated forms is not recommended. Cloves are potent. Excess intake may irritate the stomach lining, worsen acidity, or cause nausea. Eugenol can also affect blood clotting, so people on blood-thinning medications, those with liver conditions, gastritis, ulcers, or pregnant women should avoid regular use without medical advice.

claim_text: A viral Instagram reel claims that a mix of soda, coffee, Colgate toothpaste, tomato juice, and lemon juice cleans your underarms in 5 minutes and permanently prevents hair growth.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Ruby Sachdev, Consultant Aesthetic Physician at Gleneagles Hospital Bengaluru, explained that underarm darkening can occur due to several factors including frequent friction, shaving, use of certain deodorants or antiperspirants containing irritants, excessive sweating combined with bacterial buildup, medical conditions like acanthosis nigricans (often linked to insulin resistance, obesity, or hormonal imbalances), post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation from skin irritation due to shaving, waxing or other treatments, and hormonal changes during pregnancy or from disorders. These underlying factors cannot be resolved with natural remedies.

Dr Safia Tanyeem, Dermatology at Koramangala, Bengaluru, Apollo Cradle & Children's Hospital, stated: 'Laser destroys the hair root responsible for hair growth and this helps patients experience a hair free period lasting from few months to even years, with approximately 8-10 sessions done 1 month apart. However damaged hair roots regrow back under the influence of hormones and few systemic factors, and therefore results aren't permanent and patients will require maintenance shots. Compared to other methods of hair reduction, laser is safe, effective, adds to smoothness of skin and gives long-lasting results. Home remedies don't work for hair removal and instead, cause skin irritation and burns and are therefore better avoided.'

The article provides detailed scientific evidence against each ingredient:

1. Colgate toothpaste contains fluoride, abrasives, flavors, humectants, and detergents. A study by A. Skaare et al. (published in PubMed, PMID: 9176662) identified Colgate as a significant irritant causing skin erythema and other skin issues. There is no scientific evidence that it can clean underarms in five minutes or prevent hair growth or remove hair permanently.

2. A study published in Antioxidants (PMC9031248) highlighted that the topical application of tomatoes can lead to adverse skin reactions such as contact dermatitis and skin irritation including burning sensations.

3. According to a study published in Clinical and Molecular Allergy (PMC8310597), lemons are unsuitable for direct application on the skin as they can cause harm.

There are two main types of body hair: vellus hairs (shorter, thinner peach fuzz) and terminal hairs (longer, thicker hairs including underarm hair). Effective hair removal requires proven methods such as shaving, waxing, or laser treatments. Underarm darkening is often linked to underlying factors such as friction, acanthosis nigricans, genetics, or hormonal imbalances, which cannot be resolved with natural remedies.

The article also notes general health benefits of coffee (antioxidant, anti-mutagenic, anti-carcinogenic, anti-obesity effects from polyphenols like chlorogenic acids), tomatoes (lycopene, β-carotene, antioxidants reducing oxidative stress), and lemon (vitamin C, folate, potassium, used in culinary and medicinal domains), but these are nutritional/health benefits when consumed, not topical applications for hair removal. There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that the described mixture cleans underarms in 5 minutes or permanently prevents hair growth.

claim_text: Medical Dialogues reported that certain branded medicines are substandard or unsafe
doctor_explanation: Medical Dialogues had published a factual news report based on an official drug alert issued by India's drug regulator. Such alerts typically list medicines or samples that were found to be 'not of standard quality' during laboratory testing. These reports are based on regulatory data and are meant to inform healthcare professionals about quality issues identified in specific tested samples or batches, not to make broad claims about entire brands or manufacturers. The original Medical Dialogues report did not display images of branded medicines, nor did it single out entire brands as being substandard. The viral WhatsApp image has been altered to include brand names and product photos that were not part of the original report. It also falsely uses the Medical Dialogues logo, creating the misleading impression that the publication accused these brands of poor quality. This manipulation changes the meaning of the original report and turns a batch-specific regulatory update into a false allegation against entire brands. Medicine-related misinformation can cause serious harm. Misleading messages like this can create panic among patients, damage the reputation of pharmaceutical companies without evidence, and even lead people to stop prescribed medicines without medical advice. Drug quality alerts are technical, specific, and limited in scope, and misrepresenting them erodes public trust in both regulators and credible medical journalism.

claim_text: Mushrooms and chives given in soup form can cure cancer.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Tushar Patil, Senior Consultant - Medical Oncologist, Sahyadri Super Specialty Hospital, Deccan Gymkhana, Pune, explained: 'The research supporting certain mushrooms' possible anti-cancer effects is still developing, despite increased interest in this area. Polysaccharides, one of the compounds present in mushrooms, have been researched for their ability to strengthen the immune system and fight cancer. For instance, lentinan from shiitake mushrooms and PSK (polysaccharide-K) from turkey tail mushrooms have demonstrated the potential to increase chemotherapy efficacy and increase cancer patients' chances of survival. But it's crucial to handle this subject carefully. Under the advice of medical specialists, mushrooms may supplement standard cancer therapies rather than take their place. More investigation is required to comprehend their function and effectiveness in cancer therapy completely.'

Dr. Jyoti Mehta, Radiation and Clinical Oncologist, TGH Onco-Life Cancer Centre, Talegaon, added: 'Mushrooms or medicinal mushrooms are believed to cure cancer as they contain certain anti-cancer components. However, this claim hasn't been verified yet. There are no studies, research, or evidence available regarding the effectiveness of mushrooms in curing cancer. Agaricus blazei, a type of mushroom, is known to decrease the growth of cancer cells and boost the immune system. Other species of mushrooms, like reishi and maitake, have also shown potential in curing cancer. These mushrooms may carry natural components that might help prevent cancer cells from growing further, but going on hearsay is not a good idea. Don't eat mushrooms just because others are doing so or they have been promoted on social media. Mushrooms can also help strengthen the body's defense mechanism against cancer by improving the immune system and are safe to eat, they will not help you to manage cancer. One will need to undergo combination treatment, including surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy to battle cancer. You will be shocked to know that wild mushrooms are poisonous and create havoc on your health. Even those suffering from any type of food allergy should avoid mushroom intake. Furthermore, eating mushrooms mindlessly can cause liver or kidney toxicity and give a tough time to an individual. It is better to consult an expert if you are adding mushrooms to your daily diet and be assured about the quantity. Anything consumed in excess can do more harm than good. Cancer patients should strictly follow the treatment plan devised by the doctor only. Though eating mushrooms is one of the factors for cancer management, only depending on them for dealing with cancer is a strict no-no.'

The article also cites: Cancer Research UK stated 'There is no evidence that mushrooms or mushroom extract can prevent or cure cancer. Early research has shown that it may strengthen the immune system.' A Cochrane review 2016 on reishi mushrooms (Ganoderma lucidum) found a small benefit only when given with standard chemotherapy/radiotherapy treatment. Studies by Gao CM et al. showed a protective association between consumption of Allium vegetables (including Welsh onions and Chinese chives) and stomach cancer risk — a risk reduction, not a cure. According to Hye Jin Park et al., mushrooms contain anticancer components such as antroquinonol, cordycepin, hispolon, lectin, krestin, polysaccharide, sulfated polysaccharide, lentinan, and Maitake D Fraction that may minimize chemotherapy side effects, but none of these studies verify that mushrooms and/or chives can cure cancer.

claim_text: A widely circulated post from Facebook claims that a plant called chhoti dudhiya (Euphorbia thymifolia) is a simple and effective cure for jaundice. The claim advises uprooting the plant, grinding it into a paste, and consuming it with jaggery syrup twice daily. It also mentions that this home remedy can cure jaundice within 15 days.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant & HOD Gastroenterology Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, says: 'Chhoti dudhiya might be used in traditional medicine, but it hasn't been scientifically proven to cure jaundice. Jaundice is a sign that there might be a problem with your liver or bile ducts. If you rely on herbal remedies that haven't been proven to work, you could delay getting important medical help. It's really important for anyone with jaundice to see a doctor for a proper diagnosis and treatment.' Dr. Manan Arora, BAMS, Specialised in Chronic Disorders & Mental Wellness, New Delhi, explains: 'In Ayurveda, Euphorbia Thymifolia, commonly known as chhoti dudhi, is valued for its cooling properties and potential benefits for digestive health and detoxification. It may support liver function, which can be beneficial for individuals with jaundice. However, claiming it can miraculously cure jaundice within 15 days is an exaggeration.' He further explains: 'Ayurvedic practices often emphasize a holistic approach, incorporating dietary changes, herbal remedies, and lifestyle modifications to promote overall health and healing. E. thymifolia has traditional uses, like a blood purifier, sedative, hemostatic, aromatic, stimulant, astringent in diarrhea and dysentery, anthelmintic, demulcent, and laxative. It is also helpful for flatulence, constipation, chronic cough, as an antiviral in bronchial asthma and paronychia. The dried leaves and seeds are administered with buttermilk to children for bowel complaints.' Dr Arora concludes with: 'While chhoti dudhi may serve as part of a supportive regimen, jaundice generally needs comprehensive evaluation and treatment based on its underlying cause.' The article explains that there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that Euphorbia thymifolia, or any plant referred to as chhoti dudhiya, can cure jaundice. Jaundice is a medical condition caused by underlying liver issues, viral infections (like hepatitis), or blocked bile ducts, and it requires professional treatment. Even malaria can cause jaundice, especially in severe cases. Some traditional herbs may help in liver health, but no credible research proves that Euphorbia thymifolia or similar plants can completely cure jaundice in 15 days. The plant's latex can cause skin irritation, and certain plants in the Euphorbia genus contain toxic latex that can irritate the skin, eyes, and digestive system. The 2013 review found that the sap from the E. thymifolia plant can cause skin irritation and blisters in individuals with sensitive skin. Jaundice is not a disease itself but a symptom of liver dysfunction, bile duct blockage, or infections such as hepatitis. The presence of yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or fatigue needs immediate consultation with a healthcare professional. Medical professionals may prescribe antiviral medication, perform surgery for blocked bile ducts, or recommend lifestyle modifications to support liver health.

claim_text: Eating raw onions can flush out toxins and hard food particles that get stuck in the intestines, and raw onions can relieve constipation.
doctor_explanation: There are several causes of constipation, like a diet low in fibre, insufficient hydration, or a lack of physical activity. Stress, certain medications, and medical conditions like irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) can be other contributing factors. Constipation gives rise to difficulty passing stools, bloating, and discomfort. Lastly, if left untreated, it can cause complications like haemorrhoids or faecal impaction. It is important to treat constipation because chronic constipation can cause serious complications, such as rectal prolapse and faecal impaction. Maintaining regular bowel movements is important for good digestive health. Diet plays a significant role in relieving and preventing constipation. High-fibre foods, such as fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, promote bowel movements. These act by adding bulk to the stool and making it easier to pass. Drinking enough water is also important, as hydration softens stools, making them easier to eliminate. Foods like prunes (sookhaaloo bukhara), pears (nashpati), and flaxseeds (alsi ke beej) have natural laxative properties that can help relieve constipation. According to Soumam Dutta, a PhD Scholar in Nutrition from the Department of Endocrinology at the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, "Following the 'My Plate' guidelines is essential for adults to ensure adequate fibre intake, which helps prevent and treat constipation. A sustainable approach is to include a 100g salad with breakfast, lunch, and dinner. In total, a daily intake of 400g of vegetables, 100g of whole fruits, and 3-4 litres of water is recommended. Additionally, incorporating whole grains, millets, legumes, and nuts into the diet is beneficial. Bran or powdered fibre can also be added to cereals, yoghourt, or soups. Drinking warm water first thing in the morning may aid in bowel movements." He also advises, "It's important to consult a nutritionist or dietician to personalise these recommendations to your specific needs and lifestyle for optimal digestive health." Raw onions contain fibre, which is beneficial for digestion, but they are still not a treatment for constipation. While fibre supports regular bowel movements, there is no evidence to suggest that raw onions are specifically effective in relieving constipation. Additionally, for people with sensitive digestive systems, raw onions may cause gas, bloating, or discomfort, which can potentially worsen constipation. The claim that raw onions can flush out toxins is false. The body has a natural detoxification system, primarily managed by the liver and kidneys. The idea that raw onions, or any food, can "flush out toxins" from the intestines is scientifically inaccurate. While fibre in onions can support digestion, it does not have the ability to cleanse toxins from the body. This claim is misleading, as no food can single-handedly detoxify the body. Detox diets lack solid research and are often based on flawed studies with small groups and poor design. A 2015 review found no strong evidence that detox diets help with weight loss or removing toxins. Detox diets also don't explain which toxins they target or how they're removed, ignoring that the liver and kidneys already detoxify the body naturally. These diets can cause stress, increase cravings, and lead to unhealthy eating habits. Additionally, many detox products are unregulated and can be dangerous. From an Ayurveda perspective, Dr Mohit Sandhu, BAMS, Shri Shubhda Ayurveda Wellness Clinic, Gurugram states, "In Ayurvedic medicine, there is no specific evidence or traditional belief that supports the idea of raw onions 'flushing out toxins' from the intestines. Ayurveda does recognise the health benefits of onions, particularly their ability to balance certain doshas, help digestion, and provide nutrients. But, the concept of using raw onions to 'flush out toxins' is not a prominent or established practice in traditional Ayurvedic texts." Dr Sandhu further elaborates that Ayurveda emphasises a holistic approach to digestive health, combining diet, lifestyle, and herbal remedies customized to an individual's constitution (prakriti) and current state of health. Regarding the claim that raw onions can remove hard food particles stuck in the intestines - this is incorrect. The digestive system naturally breaks down food with the help of enzymes and muscular contractions known as peristalsis. There is no evidence that raw onions, or any other food, can remove hard food particles from the intestines. The claim that raw onions can flush out toxins from the intestines is false. Raw onions are a source of fibre that may support digestion. But, they do not have detoxifying properties or the ability to remove toxins or hard food particles from the intestines. Maintaining a healthy digestive system depends on a balanced diet, hydration, and regular physical activity, rather than consuming specific foods for "detox."

claim_text: BREAKING: COVID SHOTS INSTALLED NANOBOTS New Japanese study proves Pfizer and Moderna v*ccines contain unauthorized "animated worm-like" entities, invisible to the human eye, which swim, wiggle, and assemble themselves into complex structures, which cause clots inside the body. The post also claims this can cause "turbo cancer" and autoimmune diseases, referencing a study by Dr Young Mi Lee and Dr Daniel Broudy from Okinawa Christian University. The claim also involves conspiracy theories about the "Internet of Bodies" and synthetic "Biohybrid Magnetic Robots."
doctor_explanation: No, COVID-19 vaccines do not contain nanobots. The Pfizer and Moderna vaccines are built on mRNA technology, which uses lipid nanoparticles—tiny fat particles—to safely deliver mRNA into your cells. These nanoparticles are there to protect the mRNA and help it enter the cells, where it instructs them to produce the spike protein, triggering an immune response. The idea that these vaccines contain "animated worm-like" entities is entirely baseless and has no scientific support. The claim that COVID-19 vaccines include nanobots leading to "turbo cancer" and autoimmune diseases is not true as per credible evidence. These kinds of claims originate from misinformation and conspiracy theories. Research and real-world data have shown that COVID-19 vaccines are safe and effective in preventing severe illness and saving lives. The study by Dr Young Mi Lee and Dr Daniel Broudy, mentioned in the claim, has not been published in any reputable peer-reviewed journal. The International Journal of Vaccine Theory, Practice, and Research, where the claim appeared, is not recognised in the scientific community as a reliable source. No credible evidence supports their findings of "undisclosed additional engineered components" in vaccine vials. Additionally, the claim that they used 400X magnification to identify complex "nanobots" or structures is highly questionable because this level of magnification is insufficient to detect the kind of detail necessary to make such claims. The study suggests that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines contain self-assembling nanotechnology, but it was published in predatory journals like the International Journal of Vaccine Theory, Practice, and Research and shared on ResearchGate, neither of which guarantees scientific authenticity. The study does not have rigorous peer review, uses insufficient methodologies, such as low magnification, has a small and non-representative sample size, and exhibits clear bias against vaccines. The term "turbo cancer" does not exist in the medical field. The notion that vaccines could rapidly trigger aggressive cancers is not true. Similarly, there isn't enough evidence to support the idea that COVID-19 vaccines cause or worsen autoimmune diseases. A series of 2023 studies explore the potential link between COVID-19 vaccines and autoimmune reactions, noting that while some cases of new-onset autoimmune diseases have been observed post-vaccination, the risk of developing autoimmune conditions is higher with COVID-19 infection itself. The claims about the "Internet of Bodies" and "Biohybrid Magnetic Robots" controlling human bodies are rooted in conspiracy theories with no basis in medical science or vaccine technology. The "Internet of Bodies" is a hypothetical concept involving human bodies connected to the internet via devices or implants, but there is no evidence linking COVID-19 vaccines to such scenarios. The concept of Biohybrid Magnetic Microrobots is indeed new and promising for biomedical applications like targeted drug delivery, but not in the way the claim suggests. Extensive research and testing have shown that mRNA vaccines like those from Pfizer and Moderna are safe and highly effective in preventing severe illness and death from COVID-19. There are some rare but severe adverse effects associated with COVID-19 vaccines, including COVID-19 vaccine-related acute pancreatitis. All kinds of vaccines come with certain side effects. Regulatory bodies such as WHO and FDA have thoroughly reviewed these vaccines, confirming their safety and effectiveness. A 2023 review suggests that mRNA vaccines, particularly Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech, are highly safe and effective against various COVID-19 variants, outperforming traditional vaccines like Oxford-AstraZeneca and Sinopharm. These claims are not just false—they're dangerous. Deliberate misinformation like this can create fear and confusion, leading people to avoid life saving vaccines.

claim_text: Drinking coriander water induces periods within a day (4 to 5 hours). Women who suffer from PCOD or face delayed periods should try this drink. The drink also reduces cramps and prevents acne before periods.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Sandhya Rani, Senior Consultant, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Aster Women & Children Hospital, Bengaluru, told Medical Dialogues, "Coriander water may have certain medicinal benefits like reducing pain during periods because it has antispasmodic activity. It may also ease the discomfort of the women because it helps in digestion and the bloating may come down. But inducing periods is a myth because it does not have any hormonal effect. So, I do not think that taking coriander water can induce periods. It's not that easy. Periods come because of various hormonal changes. It is always suggestible to lead a good lifestyle and regularize your periods rather than using short-term solutions like coriander water."

To this Dr. Shruthi Kalagara, Consultant Obstetrician and Gynecologist at Motherhood Hospitals in Sarjapur, Bangalore added, "Let's bust this myth today. Drinking coriander seed water or any home remedy does not make your periods come. Here's the real deal. You need to ovulate first. If ovulation happens and there is no pregnancy, then your body will naturally get a period. So, instead of focusing on quick fix drinks, we need to address the root cause, whether you are ovulating regularly or not."

The article further explains: Periods (mensuration/menses) is a natural biological process involving a recurring cycle of physical and hormonal changes in the body. Typically starting between ages 12 and 15, it continues until menopause (ages 45–50). A typical menstrual period lasts 2 to 7 days and recurs every 21 to 35 days. However, around 14–25% of women experience irregular periods — periods that are unusually heavy or light, arrive too early or too late, involve intense cramping, or are unpredictable in timing. Some may miss periods for 3 to 6 months. Such irregularities are often linked to hormonal imbalances (estrogen and progesterone). Common causes include Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), contraceptive use, breastfeeding, intense physical activity, thyroid disorders, and intrauterine devices (IUDs). Lifestyle factors like obesity, stress, and smoking may also contribute.

Regarding inducing periods within a day: If a period is already due or approaching, it may begin naturally in a day. However, in cases involving PCOS, PCOD, thyroid issues, or stress-related disruptions, it is not medically feasible to induce menstruation within a single day. These conditions typically need appropriate evaluation and treatment by a healthcare professional. Additionally, if pregnancy has occurred, menstruation does not take place.

On coriander's health benefits: Coriander is valued in both culinary and traditional medicine. Coriander seeds have been traditionally used to ease pain, inflammation, and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis. The seeds are also commonly used to support digestion, relieve gas, nausea, diarrhea, and indigestion. These benefits are thought to come from coriander's ability to stimulate the liver to produce bile and digestive enzymes, enhancing digestion and gut motility.

On whether coriander water can induce periods: A review in Frontiers in Pharmacology highlights coriander's anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic effects, which could help with menstrual discomfort, but it makes no mention of regulating or triggering menstruation. A review in the International Journal of Research in Ayurveda and Pharmacy notes that coriander may aid hormone secretion and reduce menstrual pain, yet it does not link the herb to menstrual regulation. Currently, no scientific evidence confirms that coriander water can induce periods within a day, and no medical consensus endorses this claim.

claim_text: Drinking a mixture of bay leaves and apple cider vinegar (made by combining half a cup of apple cider vinegar with half a cup of water and adding 5-6 bay leaves, then refrigerating it for an hour) can dissolve gallstones and kidney stones in just three days.
doctor_explanation: Bay leaves cannot dissolve kidney or gallstones. Bay leaves may have some health benefits, such as anti-inflammatory properties, but they are not effective in dissolving kidney stones or gallstones. There is no scientific evidence that supports this claim. While bay leaves have been traditionally used in some cultures for digestive issues, their role in breaking down stones within the body is unproven. Kidney stones and gallstones are hardened deposits of minerals and substances like calcium or cholesterol, and they form over time. For a substance to dissolve these stones, it would need a specific chemical composition that can break down those deposits. Bay leaves simply do not have the necessary compounds to do this. Dr. Prerna Chaudhary, BAMS, Founder of Shri Shubhda Ayurveda Wellness Clinic in Gurugram, provided an Ayurvedic perspective: 'Ayurveda does not offer specific medicinal treatments for gallstones. However, as per Acharya Sushruta, the father of Ayurvedic Surgery, gallstones are considered a type of Shalya (foreign body) resulting from a dosha imbalance. These stones should ideally be removed through Shalya Karma (surgical management). For gallstones measuring less than 3-4 mm (Pitta-Ashmari), Ayurvedic medicines prescribed by a trained Ayurvedic practitioner can help dissolve them.' Dr. Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, Consultant Nephrologist at Narayana Health City, Bengaluru, explained that kidney stones are common in tropical countries due to dehydration, and treatment depends on the stone type.
